title: Efficacy and Safety of Consecutive Use of 1% and 0.01% Atropine for Myopia Control in Chinese Children: The Atropine for Children and Adolescent Myopia Progression Study

groups.description: Group A: 1% atropine sulfate eye gel once weekly in both eyes (after a 1-week daily loading dose) for 6 months, then switched to 0.01% atropine nightly at the 6-month (24-week) visit; extracted up to the switch; 91 completers with good compliance of 104 randomised; Shanghai Eye Disease Prevention and Treatment Centre, China; mean age of the completers (Table 1)
Group B: 0.01% atropine sulfate eyedrops once nightly in both eyes for 1 year; 80 completers with good compliance of 103 randomised; Shanghai, China; mean age of the completers (Table 1)

notes: Randomised, controlled, non-masked trial (ACAMP, NCT03949101), May 2019 to August 2020, Shanghai Eye Disease Prevention and Treatment Centre, China; 207 children aged 6-12 years randomised 1:1 (Group A 104, Group B 103).

Analysis set: children who completed 1 year with good compliance (adherence of at least 80%): Group A 91 (87.5% of randomised), Group B 80 (77.7%); both at least 70% (protocol inclusion 5), so admitted; baseline values of this set are tabulated in Table 1 ('Completed 1 year').
Visits at 1, 12, 24 and 48 weeks; the 36-week visit was cancelled because of COVID-19. Table 2 '6 months' and '12 months' are the 24- and 48-week visits and are converted as weeks x 7/30.4375 months.
Only right eyes were analysed (Statistical Analysis).
Axial length by IOL-Master 700; lens power, anterior chamber depth, lens thickness and corneal power are also tabulated, not extracted.
Photochromic and reading-add (presbyopic) glasses were provided to children with glare or near-vision difficulty.
